title: Restore governed ai-start after malformed foreign worktree identity deadlock
outOfScope: Cleaning, editing, or deleting any foreign linked worktree.
Modifying Work Item #664 evidence or archive.
Implementing #668 PR critical-coverage or post-archive recovery behavior.
Merging, releasing, or deleting branches outside this Work Item lifecycle.

sources.reason: The governed start command currently fails closed before a corrective Contract can be created.
Existing lifecycle-start regression coverage defines compatible behavior.
Corrective issue records the systemic ai-start identity deadlock.

rawUserRequest: Create corrective Issue #669 and restore standard governed starts: ai-start cannot create its own corrective Contract because an unrelated dirty malformed linked worktree has a branch/task identity mismatch. User authorizes narrowly scoped automation that writes only #669 evidence and performs no foreign cleanup.

riskAssessment.reason: The correction changes fail-closed start behavior and must preserve foreign evidence integrity.

reasons: A systemic lifecycle deadlock blocks creation of corrective Work Items.

executionDecision.reason: User authorized only the self-contained bootstrap necessary to restore standard governed starts.

preReviewWarnings: Bootstrap is limited to #669 Contract, Summary, and Start Receipt; implementation must restore normal ai-start behavior without foreign cleanup.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record immutable implementation and finish checkpoints for this high-risk lifecycle correction.

acceptance: A malformed or dirty foreign linked worktree cannot permanently prevent an unrelated dedicated branch from creating its own governed corrective Work Item.
The corrective start path is bounded to self-owned Contract, Summary, Start Receipt, and generated status evidence and performs no foreign cleanup or mutation.
Ordinary ai-start retains fail-closed validation for ambiguous active Work Item identity and reports a governed recovery route.
Regression coverage proves the original malformed-foreign-worktree deadlock and the restored standard-start behavior.
Lifecycle documentation explains the recovery boundary without weakening normal branch/task identity enforcement.
guidelines: Preserve foreign Work Item evidence and worktrees without mutation.
Use executable tests for every recovery boundary.
Keep recovery authorization explicit and limited to the corrective Work Item.

intent.problem: A malformed, dirty unrelated linked worktree causes ai-start to fail before it can create a Contract for the corrective Work Item needed to repair that condition.
constraints: Only #669 evidence may be created during bootstrap.
No foreign cleanup, mutation, archive change, merge, or release.
intent.rationale: A self-only bootstrap breaks the governance deadlock while preserving the normal fail-closed start rule until the corrective implementation restores a standard route.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: An unrelated malformed linked worktree blocks ordinary ai-start before Contract creation.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The standard path remains fail-closed and the governed recovery route is explicit.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Create the malformed foreign identity fixture and assert the normal start denial plus the bounded recovery behavior.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A valid dedicated Work Item starts while foreign evidence remains untouched.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Only the new Work Item's Contract, Summary, Start Receipt, and generated status are written.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Compare foreign fixture bytes before and after start, then assert the new Work Item evidence is self-owned.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: No restricted paths are approved for this bootstrap.

rollbackNote: Revert the #669 Work Item diff; do not alter foreign Work Item evidence or worktrees.
